questions.question: Keshav invests a sum of ₹5400 and Tushar invests a sum of ₹10200 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 3 years, Tushar gets ₹360 more interest than Keshav, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in principal amounts = ₹10200 − ₹5400 = ₹4800

Difference in simple interest for 3 years = ₹360

Difference in interest for 1 year = 360 ÷ 3 = ₹120

Rate of interest = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Difference in principal) × 100

Rate = (120 ÷ 4800) × 100 = 2.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 2.5%.**

⇒ Taking common factors out:

⇒ x = √[6(2 + √2) × 4(2 − √2)]

Mean Proportional

For two numbers a and b, the mean proportional is the square root of their product. Formula: x = √(ab).

Third Proportional

For two numbers a and b, the third proportional c satisfies a : b = b : c. Formula: c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers a, b and c, the fourth proportional d satisfies a : b = c : d. Formula: d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Algebraic Identity

The product of the sum and difference of two terms is given by (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².
</p

questions.question: A, B and C can complete a piece of work in 12, 20 and 15 days, respectively. A, B and C will complete the work while working on alternate days. C works on the 1st day, B works on the 2nd day and A works on the 3rd day and so on. In how many days will the work get complete?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(12, 20, 15) = 60 units.

Efficiencies: A = 5, B = 3, C = 4 units/day.

Sequence is C, B, A → Work in 1 cycle (3 days) = 4 + 3 + 5 = 12 units.

Number of 3-day cycles = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 cycles.

Total days = 5 × 3 = 15 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 12 days

Time taken by B = 20 days

Time taken by C = 15 days

**Concept Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual times taken.

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ According to the question, they work on alternate days in the sequence C, B, A.

⇒ Work done by C on the 1st day = 4 units

⇒ Work done by B on the 2nd day = 3 units

⇒ Work done by A on the 3rd day = 5 units

⇒ Total work done in one 3-day cycle = 4 + 3 + 5 = 12 units

⇒ Number of complete cycles required = Total Work ÷ Work per cycle

⇒ Number of complete cycles = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 cycles

⇒ Total time required = 5 cycles × 3 days/cycle = 15 days

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work

Work is completed in repeated cycles. Always calculate the total work done in one full cycle, then divide the total work by this value to find the number of full cycles. Compute any remaining work day-by-day according to the sequence.

Work and Wages

Wages are strictly proportional to the total amount of work done by each individual. If all individuals work for the exact same number of days, the wages can be directly divided in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Negative Work (Pipes & Cisterns)

In problems involving a leak or an emptying pipe, its efficiency is taken as negative. Total combined efficiency = Efficiency of filling pipes − Efficiency of emptying pipes.
</p

questions.question: 33 guava trees, 55 banana trees and 88 malta trees need to be planted in rows such that each row contains the same number of trees of one type only. The minimum number of rows in which the trees may be planted is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To minimize the number of rows, each row must contain the maximum possible number of identical trees.

Maximum trees per row = HCF(33, 55, 88) = 11 trees.

Minimum number of rows = Total Trees ÷ Trees per row

⇒ Rows = (33 + 55 + 88) ÷ 11 = 176 ÷ 11 = 16 rows.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 rows.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Number of guava trees = 33

Number of banana trees = 55

Number of malta trees = 88

**Concept Used:**

To keep the number of rows to an absolute minimum, each row must contain the greatest possible number of trees. This requires finding the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the separate tree quantities.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Finding the HCF of 33, 55, and 88:

⇒ 33 = 3 × 11

⇒ 55 = 5 × 11

⇒ 88 = 2³ × 11

⇒ HCF (33, 55, 88) = 11

⇒ Thus, each row will perfectly contain 11 trees of the same type.

Now, calculate the individual row counts:

⇒ Rows of guava trees = 33 ÷ 11 = 3 rows

⇒ Rows of banana trees = 55 ÷ 11 = 5 rows

⇒ Rows of malta trees = 88 ÷ 11 = 8 rows

⇒ Minimum total rows = 3 + 5 + 8 = 16 rows

**∴ The correct answer is 16 rows.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The HCF is the largest positive integer that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder. It is widely used in division and grouping problems to maximize the size of equal groups.

Application of HCF in Real-life Grouping

Whenever diverse items need to be arranged into the minimum possible identical rows or containers without mixing them, the quantity per group should equal their HCF. The minimum number of groups is found by the formula: (Total sum of all items) ÷ HCF.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

Contrasting with HCF, LCM finds the smallest multiple common to the numbers. It is primarily applied in synchronization problems, like finding when distinct events will repeat together.
</p

questions.question: LCM and HCF of two numbers are 154 and 7 respectively. If one of the numbers is 77, then find the other number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the standard property: **Product of two numbers = LCM × HCF**

Let the unknown number be x.

77 × x = 154 × 7

x = (154 ÷ 77) × 7

x = 2 × 7 = 14

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of two numbers = 154

HCF of two numbers = 7

First number (A) = 77

**Formula Used:**

For any two positive integers A and B:

A × B = LCM(A, B) × HCF(A, B)

**Calculations:**

Let the second number be B.

⇒ 77 × B = 154 × 7

⇒ B = (154 × 7) ÷ 77

⇒ B = 154 ÷ 77 × 7

⇒ B = 2 × 7

⇒ B = 14

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF of Fractions

LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators).
HCF of fractions = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators).

Co-prime Numbers Property

If two numbers are co-prime (their HCF is 1), then their LCM is always equal to their product.

Product Rule Limitation

The mathematical rule (Product of numbers = LCM × HCF) is valid ONLY for exactly two numbers. It cannot be applied to three or more numbers.
</p

questions.question: Applied to a bill of ₹600, the difference between a single discount of 25% and two successive discounts of 10% and 15% is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference between a single discount of (A + B)% and two successive discounts of A% and B% is exactly **(A × B) ÷ 100 %** of the marked price.

Here, A = 10 and B = 15.

Difference % = (10 × 15) ÷ 100 % = 150 ÷ 100 % = 1.5%

Difference in Amount = 1.5% of ₹600 = (1.5 ÷ 100) × 600 = ₹9

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9.**

questions.question: Find the volume of a hemisphere of radius 6√3 cm.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The volume of a hemisphere is calculated directly using the formula V = (2/3) × πr³.

Given the radius r = 6√3 cm, substitute the value into the formula:

V = (2/3) × π × (6√3)³

V = (2/3) × π × (216 × 3√3)

V = (2/3) × π × 648√3 = 432√3π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 432√3π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 

 

 
 
• 
 r = 6√3 cm
 
• 
 h = r

**Given:**

Radius of the hemisphere (r) = 6√3 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Hemisphere = (2/3) × πr³

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, find the cube of the radius:

⇒ r³ = (6√3)³

⇒ r³ = 6³ × (√3)³ = 216 × 3√3 = 648√3

⇒ Now, substitute this value into the volume formula:

⇒ Volume = (2/3) × π × 648√3

⇒ Volume = 2 × 216√3 × π

⇒ Volume = 432√3π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 432√3π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Hemisphere

The total surface area includes the curved base and the flat circular top. It is given by TSA = 3πr².

Curved Surface Area of Hemisphere

The area of only the curved outer dome, excluding the base, is given by CSA = 2πr².

Volume of a Sphere

A hemisphere is exactly half of a full sphere. The volume of a full sphere is V = (4/3) × πr³.
</p

questions.question: Prakhar goes from his home to school at a speed of 24 km/hr and returns at the speed of 36 km/hr. Find the average speed for the whole journey.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When the distance traveled is the same for both parts of the journey, the average speed is calculated directly:

Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

Average Speed = (2 × 24 × 36) ÷ (24 + 36)

⇒ 1728 ÷ 60 = 28.8 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 28.8 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed to school (S₁) = 24 km/hr

Speed returning home (S₂) = 36 km/hr

Let the one-way distance be D km.

 
 Home
 
 
 School

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 
• 
 24 km/hr
 
 
• 
 36 km/hr

 

 

 

 Distance = D

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = D + D = 2D

⇒ Time taken to reach school = D ÷ 24

⇒ Time taken to return home = D ÷ 36

⇒ Total Time = (D ÷ 24) + (D ÷ 36)

⇒ Total Time = (3D + 2D) ÷ 72 = 5D ÷ 72

⇒ Average Speed = 2D ÷ (5D ÷ 72)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 72) ÷ 5 = 144 ÷ 5

⇒ Average Speed = 28.8 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 28.8 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Different Distances)

If distances are different, Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = (D₁ + D₂ + ...) ÷ (T₁ + T₂ + ...).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂. When moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Distance and Speed Relation

If distance is constant, the ratio of time taken is inversely proportional to the ratio of speeds (T₁:T₂ = S₂:S₁).

Average Speed of 3 Equal Distances

If a person covers 3 equal distances at speeds x, y, and z, the Average Speed = (3xyz) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).
</p

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper promises to sell his goods at cost price. However, he uses a weight that actually weighs 39% less than what is written on it. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a dishonest dealer selling at cost price, Profit % = [ Error ÷ (True Value − Error) ] × 100

Given Error = 39% and True Value = 100%

⇒ Profit % = [ 39 ÷ (100 − 39) ] × 100

⇒ Profit % = (39 ÷ 61) × 100 = 3900 ÷ 61

⇒ Profit % = 63 ⁵⁷/₆₁ %

**∴ The correct answer is 63 ⁵⁷/₆₁ %.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 Dishonest Dealer Profit Logic

 
 Actual: 61g
 CP = 61
 
 
 Claimed: 100g
 SP = 100

 

 

 Profit = 39

 Profit % = (39 ÷ 61) × 100 = 63 57/61 %

**Given:**

Shopkeeper sells goods at cost price.

He uses a weight that is 39% less than the marked weight.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the cost price of 100g of goods be ₹100.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) of the claimed 100g = ₹100.

⇒ However, actual weight given = 100 − 39 = 61g.

⇒ Actual Cost Price (CP) for 61g of goods = ₹61.

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 100 − 61 = ₹39.

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (39 ÷ 61) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 3900 ÷ 61 = 63 ⁵⁷/₆₁ %

**∴ The correct answer is 63 ⁵⁷/₆₁ %.**

**__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Selling at CP

When a dealer claims to sell goods at cost price but uses false weight, Profit % = (Error ÷ True Weight Given) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer Selling at Markup

If the dealer marks up the price by x% and also gives less weight, use Successive Percentage or Ratio method connecting (Actual CP → SP) and (Actual Weight → Claimed Weight).

Successive Discount

Equivalent discount for two successive discounts of a% and b% is [ a + b − (a × b ÷ 100) ]%.

questions.question: The average age of 57 students of a class is 13 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 14 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By using the net change method for averages:

Teacher's age = Old Average + (Total Number of Persons × Increase in Average)

Total persons after teacher joins = 57 + 1 = 58

Increase in average = 14 − 13 = 1 year

Teacher's age = 13 + (58 × 1) = 71 years

**∴ The correct answer is 71 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students = 57

Average age of 57 students = 13 years

New average age including the teacher = 14 years

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

 
 57 Students (Avg = 13)
 
 
 Teacher (Age = ?)

 

 New Avg = 14 (Increase of +1 year)

 Teacher's Age = 13 + (58 × 1) = 71

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of 57 students = 57 × 13 = 741 years

⇒ Total number of people after including the teacher = 57 + 1 = 58

⇒ Total age of 58 people = 58 × 14 = 812 years

⇒ Age of the teacher = Total age of 58 people − Total age of 57 students

⇒ Age of the teacher = 812 − 741 = 71 years

**∴ The correct answer is 71 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

New Member Joining

When a new member joins a group: New Value = Old Average + (New Total Number of Members × Change in Average).

Member Leaving

When a member leaves a group: Left Value = Old Average − (Remaining Number of Members × Change in Average).

Replacement in a Group

When one member replaces another: New Member's Value = Replaced Member's Value + (Total Members × Change in Average).

Weighted Average

The combined average of two groups with sizes n₁ and n₂ and averages A₁ and A₂ is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
</p

questions.question: The speed of a stream is 4 km/h. A boat can go 20 km downstream and 14 km upstream in 3 hours. What is the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Time = Distancedₒwₙ ÷ (Speedbₒₐₜ + Speedₛₜᵣₑₐₘ) + Distanceᵤₚ ÷ (Speedbₒₐₜ − Speedₛₜᵣₑₐₘ)

Substitute Option 1 (12 km/h) into the equation directly to verify the total time.

⇒ Total Time = 20 ÷ (12 + 4) + 14 ÷ (12 − 4)

⇒ Total Time = 20 ÷ 16 + 14 ÷ 8 = 1.25 + 1.75 = 3 hours (Matches Given Time).

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of stream = 4 km/h

Distance downstream = 20 km, Distance upstream = 14 km

Total time taken = 3 hours

 
 Downstream Journey
 Dist = 20 km | Speed = x + 4
 
 
 Upstream Journey
 Dist = 14 km | Speed = x − 4

 

 

 
 
 Total Time
 3 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Downstream Speed = Speed of boat + Speed of stream

Upstream Speed = Speed of boat − Speed of stream

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the boat in still water be x km/h.

⇒ Downstream speed = (x + 4) km/h

⇒ Upstream speed = (x − 4) km/h

⇒ 20 ÷ (x + 4) + 14 ÷ (x − 4) = 3

⇒ [20(x − 4) + 14(x + 4)] ÷ [(x + 4)(x − 4)] = 3

⇒ (20x − 80 + 14x + 56) ÷ (x² − 16) = 3

⇒ 34x − 24 = 3(x² − 16)

⇒ 3x² − 48 = 34x − 24

⇒ 3x² − 34x − 24 = 0

⇒ 3x² − 36x + 2x − 24 = 0

⇒ 3x(x − 12) + 2(x − 12) = 0

⇒ (3x + 2)(x − 12) = 0

⇒ x = 12 or x = −2/3

Since speed cannot be negative, x = 12 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

It is the average of the downstream and upstream speeds: B = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

It is half the difference between the downstream and upstream speeds: S = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed of Journey

If a boat goes a certain distance downstream and returns the same distance upstream, the average speed is (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).
</p

questions.question: Sachin has two grandsons Chetan and Vipul. 13 year old Chetan gets some money from Sachin’s wealth and 14 year old Vipul gets rest of the money. But Chetan and Vipul will get money only when they turn 23 years old. Till then the money is in a bank getting interest at rate 8% compounded annually. When both turn 23, they receive the same amount. How much had Sachin given Vipul (in ₹) initially, if total money with Sachin was ₹23400?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal amounts under compound interest, the ratio of shares of the older person to the younger person is (1 + R/100)ΔT.

Difference in time (ΔT) = 14 − 13 = 1 year.

Share ratio (Vipul : Chetan) = (1 + 8/100)¹ : 1 = 108/100 : 1 = 27 : 25.

Vipul's share = [27 ÷ (27 + 25)] × 23400 = (27 ÷ 52) × 23400 = 12150.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12150.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total money = ₹23400

Rate of interest (R) = 8% p.a. compounded annually

Chetan's time (T₁) = 23 − 13 = 10 years

Vipul's time (T₂) = 23 − 14 = 9 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount A = P(1 + R/100)T

 
 Total: ₹23400

 
• 
 
• 

 
 Chetan's Share (C)
 Time = 10 yrs
 Rate = 8% CI

 
 Vipul's Share (V)
 Time = 9 yrs
 Rate = 8% CI

 
• 
 
• 

 
 Final Amounts are Equal

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Chetan's share be C and Vipul's share be V.

⇒ C(1 + 8/100)¹⁰ = V(1 + 8/100)⁹

⇒ C(108/100)¹⁰ = V(108/100)⁹

⇒ V ÷ C = (108/100)¹⁰ ÷ (108/100)⁹

⇒ V ÷ C = 108 / 100 = 27 / 25

⇒ Ratio of Vipul's share to Chetan's share = 27 : 25

⇒ Total ratio parts = 27 + 25 = 52 parts

⇒ 52 parts = ₹23400

⇒ 1 part = 23400 ÷ 52 = ₹450

⇒ Vipul's share = 27 parts = 27 × 450 = ₹12150

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12150.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equal Amount Distribution under CI

When a sum is divided between two individuals such that their amounts become equal after different time periods, the ratio of their original shares is determined by (1 + R/100)ΔT. The person with less time remaining (older) receives a larger initial share.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest is calculated only on the initial principal. In Compound Interest, the interest earned is added back to the principal at each compounding interval, leading to exponential growth. For the first compounding period, SI and CI remain identical.
